why.title: Ship fires are a different battlefield
why.description: For cruise ships, cargo vessels, offshore platforms, and high-speed craft, fire is the second-greatest threat after sinking. Narrow compartments, vertical passages, enclosed engine rooms, and hot metal structures demand tactics entirely different from land-based building fires.
why.lead: Firefighters often enter at the hottest point and work downward — this reverse-advancement logic only becomes muscle memory through repeated drills in realistic hull structures.
why.body: TZJ maritime training facilities are modeled on real vessels, integrating bridge, engine room, cargo holds, ship doors, and gangways so teams build real skills on land before going to sea.

props.title: Bridge / Wheelhouse
props.desc: Authentic bridge layout with blackout windows for compartment search and command coordination in heavy smoke.

props.title: Ship Ladder / Hatch
props.desc: Vertical passages between decks with steep ship ladders and hatches for boarding, vertical transfer, and casualty movement in tight spaces.

props.title: Ship Door (Multi-latch)
props.desc: Six-latch and other ship door styles for opening, forcing, and advancing through compartments.

props.title: Engine-Room Fire
props.desc: Hot, confined engine rooms and flange fire simulators for suppression, cooling, and evacuation in complex environments.

props.title: Reconfigurable Maze
props.desc: Track-free maze panels reconfigurable inside compartments for search and orientation in low visibility.

props.title: Cargo / Storage Hold
props.desc: Cargo holds, storage compartments, and porthole props for cargo fire and confined-space search and rescue.

extraFeatures: Full-loop protection systems with isolation valves
